paper_title: AttentionInfluence Adopting Attention Head Influence for Weak-to-Strong   Pretraining Data Selection
caption: The statistics of clustering. The left is the clustering result of AttentionInfluence, the right part is that of FineWeb-Edu Classifier.
model_annotation: This figure presents two side-by-side pie charts comparing the clustering results of two methods: AttentionInfluence (left) and FineWeb-Edu Classifier (right), each displaying the distribution of data across various topic categories. Both charts use a sunburst-like structure with an inner ring showing broader groupings and an outer ring showing finer subcategories, with numerical values (likely percentages) labeled for each slice. The AttentionInfluence chart contains approximately 20 categories, with the largest slices being Education (25, shown in green), History & Society (23, shown in blue), Health & Medicine (22, shown in blue), Teaching & resources (15, shown in green), Science (15, shown in pink/red), Animal & Plant (13, shown in orange), Tech & Engineer (12, shown in orange), Diseases (11, shown in light blue), Science & technology education (10, shown in green), and Society & culture (10, shown in blue), followed by smaller slices for Historical review (7), Events & people (6), Medical (6), Nutrition (5), Infor tech (5), Emerging tech (4), Fin & Law (3), Materials (3), Manage (2), and Policy (1). The FineWeb-Edu Classifier chart shows a notably different distribution, with Education being the dominant category at 38 (shown in green), followed by Science & technology education (19, green), Health & Medicine (19, blue), History & Society (19, orange), Teaching & resources (17, green), Science (15, pink/red), Animal & Plant (12, orange), Historical review (12, blue), Diseases (10, light blue), Tech & Engineer (8, orange), Nutrition (7), Society & culture (5), Emerging tech (4), Infor tech (3), Materials (3), Medical (2), Events & people (2), Healthy education (2), Materials (1), and Manage (1). Both charts use consistent color coding for broader category groupings—green tones for education-related topics, blue for health and history-related topics, orange for science and technology, and pink/red for science—and include labels with numerical values placed either inside or connected via leader lines to their respective slices. The slices in both charts do not appear to be ordered strictly by size but rather grouped thematically within the inner ring categories.
